Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines finite tensoring, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space of dimension $d\ge0$,
let $n\ge0$, and let $E:=V^{\otimes n}$ carry the commuting left place action
of $S_n$ and diagonal action of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$
([[def-commuting-symmetric-and-linear-actions-on-tensor-power]]). Let
$B:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{g^{\otimes n}:g\in\operatorname{GL}(V)\}$,
and for $\lambda\vdash n$ put
$$M_\lambda:=\operatorname{Hom}_{S_n}\bigl(S^\lambda,E\bigr),$$
on which $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ acts by postcomposition
$(g\cdot\psi)(s):=g^{\otimes n}\psi(s)$ and $B$ acts by
$b\cdot\psi:=b\circ\psi$. Then:

1. **(Decomposition.)** There is an isomorphism of
   $(S_n\times\operatorname{GL}(V))$-modules
   $$E\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n,\ \ell(\lambda)\le d}S^\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,$$
   where $S_n$ acts on the first factor and trivially on $M_\lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ acts on $M_\lambda$ by postcomposition and trivially
   on $S^\lambda$. The sum runs over exactly the partitions $\lambda\vdash n$
   with at most $d$ rows.
2. **(Nonzero irreducible factors.)** For every $\lambda\vdash n$ with
   $\ell(\lambda)\le d$ the space $M_\lambda$ is nonzero and irreducible as a
   module over $B$ by postcomposition, hence also irreducible as a
   $\operatorname{GL}(V)$-module and as a $\mathfrak{gl}(V)$-module under
   $x\mapsto\Delta(x)$
   ([[def-irreducible-completely-reducible-and-faithful-lie-algebra-representation]]);
   for $\ell(\lambda)>d$ one has $M_\lambda=0$.
3. **(Pairwise inequivalence of the nonzero factors.)** If $\lambda\ne\mu$
   are partitions of $n$ with $\ell(\lambda)\le d$ and $\ell(\mu)\le d$, then
   $M_\lambda$ and $M_\mu$ are non-isomorphic as $B$-modules, as
   $\operatorname{GL}(V)$-modules and as $\mathfrak{gl}(V)$-modules. Thus the
   nonzero factors in the decomposition of claim 1 are pairwise inequivalent,
   and a nonzero $M_\lambda$ is not isomorphic to a zero $M_\mu$ with
   $\ell(\mu)>d$ because their dimensions differ; no assertion is made about
   two zero factors.
4. **(Highest weight $\lambda$.)** For every $\lambda\vdash n$ with
   $\ell(\lambda)\le d$, writing $\lambda_i:=0$ for $i>\ell(\lambda)$, the
   module $M_\lambda$ has highest weight $\lambda$ with respect to the Borel
   of upper triangular matrices: it contains a nonzero vector $\varphi$ with
   $\Delta(E_{ii})\circ\varphi=\lambda_i\varphi$ for all $i$ and
   $\Delta(E_{ij})\circ\varphi=0$ for all $i<j$, and every nonzero
   $\psi\in M_\lambda$ killed by all raising operators $\Delta(E_{ij})$,
   $i<j$, and satisfying $\Delta(E_{ii})\circ\psi=\mu_i\psi$ for scalars
   $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_d$ satisfies $\mu=\lambda$ and lies in
   $\mathbb C\varphi$.
5. **(Homogeneous polynomial module of degree $n$.)** Fix a basis
   $e_1,\dots,e_d$ of $V$ and write $ge_j=\sum_ig_{ij}e_i$ for the matrix
   entries of $g\in\operatorname{GL}(V)$. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ with
   $\ell(\lambda)\le d$ and every basis of $M_\lambda$, each matrix
   coefficient $g\mapsto\langle\psi^*,g\cdot\psi\rangle$ of the action on
   $M_\lambda$ is a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ in the entries
   $g_{ij}$.

All statements are over $\mathbb C$.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], with source
parameter $s$, monomial basis $M_A$, ordinary bar $\psi$, source
dual-canonical family $L_A$, canonical family $T_A$, and the source forms
$\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$.

The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$, and there is its normalized module projection
$\pi:F(\Lambda)\to V(\Lambda)$.

(1) The vectors $S_A:=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of
$V(\Lambda)$, and $D_A:=\pi L_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ form the
**source dual-canonical basis** of $V(\Lambda)$.

(2) What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish
for nonstandard $A$. The integral kernel of $\pi$ is the saturated direct
summand with basis the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and
$\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on
$\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$,
$$\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$$
which gives the explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials.

(3) All bases and maps commute with upper cuts and common-tail embeddings, so
the assertions hold in the full direct limit. The relation of the source
$D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family
([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]) is the explicit weight
rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison, not an unqualified
identification.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and $I$ bounded below. The
standard-class map $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ identifies the direct-sum $K_0$ of the
genuine tableau parabolic blocks with the full integral Fock module, with
matching multiset degrees and the residue Chevalley action of
$\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$. For every projective $P$ and finite-length $N$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle\quad\text{at }s=1 .$$
In particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; no false standard/simple
orthogonality $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$ is asserted. The projective,
simple and tilting basis identifications are proved separately.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For $I$ bounded below use
the actual finite classical tableau-block dictionary of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
including repeated entries. Fix the right place action $(a w)_i=a_{w(i)}$. Let
$w_A$ be shortest with $a(A)w_A$ weakly increasing, and let $K$ be the Young
stabilizer of that sorted multiset. Then $w_A$ is shortest RIGHT modulo $K$,
$d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest LEFT, and
$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,\,w_B}(s^{-2}).$$
This is the **antispherical/sign** family for the entry stabilizer, in the left
convention after inversion, with Hecke variable $v=s$; the library quantum
parameter is instead $t=s^{-1}$. It has support $A\le B$ and diagonal $1$, and
$d$ is its inverse coefficient matrix through $p(-s)$. The **column Levi**
subgroup $J$ is generally different from $K$. The genuine parabolic block
composition matrix is
$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\mathrm{col}}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,\,d(A)w_0}(1),$$
where $C$ runs over the column permutations of $B$. This uses singular ordinary
**spherical** coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi
cancellation, so it covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does
not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic $\mathcal O$ and does
not identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The exact residue
functors of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] on the
genuine finite-$n$ parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free
generalized-standard flags given by the valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and
$i+1\to i$.

(1) Their $K_0$ operators are the full integrable $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock
Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the
standard basis.

(2) For each simple $L(A)$, a residue translate vanishes exactly when the
corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual
indecomposable with simple equal head and socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$, respectively
$L(\tilde e_iA)$.

(3) The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the
ground-state class, with
$M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one
highest constituent.

No action on labels alone proves the $K_0$ relations or the head/socle
statement.

Assume AC. Work in genuine type-$A$ parabolic category $\mathcal O$ for
$\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its fixed Borel. Its column Levi has ordered
blocks of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. All entries in column $j$ lie in
$c_j+\mathbb Z$, where the original admissibility condition is
$c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z\Rightarrow c_j=c_k$. Use the source highest-weight
convention $\eta_i=a_i+i-1$ and half-sum
$\rho_i=(N+1-2i)/2$, with the column reading prescribed by the source Borel.
For each occurring entry coset $\kappa$ retain its columns in their original
order. Fix an order on the finite set of cosets; no order on $\mathbb C$ is used.

Subject to the local HC tensor-projective comparison stated in [F1], stable
sorting of the coordinates by $\kappa$ gives an exact, complex-linear
equivalence of the genuine parabolic categories, carrying each ordinary
Verma label by the dot permutation and carrying the corresponding generalized
standard, simple head and projective cover. On each linkage block, the sorted
category is equivalent to the product of the corresponding parabolic blocks
for $\mathfrak{gl}_{N_\kappa}$, where
$N_\kappa=\sum_{j\in\kappa}q_j$. Product means the abelian category generated
by finite presentations of outer tensor products, equivalently modules over
the tensor product of the finite block endomorphism algebras.

For the original pyramid with $n$ rows put $n_\kappa=\max_{j\in\kappa}q_j$.
The component integral entry dictionary is exactly
$$a_i^{\mathrm{int}}=a_i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa,\qquad m_j=q_j-n_\kappa,\qquad \inf I_\kappa=1-n_\kappa.$$
Thus $m_j+1-\inf I_\kappa=q_j$, with the original nonincreasing retained
heights and charges. For the admitted-ground subcategories, where each original entry has a
nonnegative integral difference from its own ground entry, this dictionary
lands in the bounded-below admitted integral component models of [F4]. For
other genuine parabolic blocks it records the integral weight/coset
dictionary and the trace shift, without asserting membership in that fixed
admitted cut. If the component follows $B_\kappa$ sorted coordinates, its
Levi highest weight and the integral highest weight differ by the scalar
trace-character shift
$$\delta_\kappa=B_\kappa+c_\kappa-n+n_\kappa.$$
This shift is a Lie algebra character and requires no integrality of
$c_\kappa$. Singular repeated-entry linkage blocks are included. The original
complex origins, component entry multisets and their scalar centres remain
recorded; different complex cosets are not merged into one integral block.

Sorting commutes coherently with finite tensoring and its invariant Casimir
and permutation maps. The separated product decomposition is blockwise and
does not assert that unrestricted tensoring is componentwise. The proof gives
its actual filtration and block-projection comparison. Choices of sorting
word with the same stable permutation yield the natural comparison fixed on
the chosen reference highest vector and its tensor-projective presentations.

Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and fix $n\ge1$ together with a shift matrix
$\sigma=(s_{i,j})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ of nonnegative integers satisfying
$s_{i,j}+s_{j,k}=s_{i,k}$ whenever $i\le j\le k$ or $i\ge j\ge k$, and
$s_{i,i}=0$. The **shifted Yangian** $Y_n(\sigma)$ is the associative unital
$\mathbb C$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) generated by the
shifted Drinfeld generators $D_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $r\ge1$),
$E_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i,i+1}$), and
$F_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<n$, $r>s_{i+1,i}$). For $i<j$, the higher-root
coefficients $E_{i,j}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{i,j}$ and
$F_{j,i}^{(r)}$ have range $r>s_{j,i}$; they are defined recursively by
adjacent-root commutators, not declared as a duplicate independent family.
These generators are subject to the shifted Drinfeld relations of the source (the
shifted analogues of the $D$-$D$, $D$-$E$, $D$-$F$, $E$-$E$, $F$-$F$ and
$E$-$F$ relations, with the shift matrix $\sigma$ entering through the ranges
and the constants). Two filtrations are fixed on it: the **canonical
filtration**, in which each generator of upper index $r$ has degree $r$, and
the **loop filtration**, in which it has degree $r-1$; their associated
graded algebras are different (the canonical one is commutative polynomial,
the loop one is a current algebra).

For the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with conjugate
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$ ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]])
the relevant shift matrix is $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$
for $i\ge j$, and the **type-A finite W-algebra** is the quotient
$$W(\lambda)=Y_n(\sigma)/\bigl(D_1^{(r)},\ r>p_1\bigr)$$
of $Y_n(\sigma)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the higher modes of
$D_1$ beyond $p_1$.

Write the Gauss decomposition $T(u)=F(u)D(u)E(u)$ of the generating matrix,
with $T(u)=\sum_{r\ge0}T_{i,j}^{(r)}u^{-r}$, $T_{i,j}^{(0)}=\delta_{i,j}$, and
**no** additional factor $u^{s_{i,j}}$: the coefficient of $u^{-r}$ is the
mode $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$. Its modes satisfy $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$0<r\le s_{i,j}$, and in the finite quotient also $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$r>S_{i,j}:=s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$, so the finite quotient has the PBW basis
of ordered monomials
$$T_{i,j}^{(r)},\qquad s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}.$$
The auxiliary signed path polynomials used in the source to construct the
Gauss generators are not all identified with these shifted $T$-modes; the root
of $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ is the weight $\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j$, and the
surviving modes have loop leading term $(-1)^{r-1}e_{i,j;r-1}$ in the
centralizer basis of the pyramid.

derivations.claim: **The categorical nonstandard kernel.** In the Fock $L/D$ bases the normalized projection is a coordinate projection with coefficients $0,1$, so specialization at $1$ has precisely the off-standard span as kernel. Module-linearity makes this kernel stable under every $E_i,F_i$. Under [F3], expand $[f_iL(A)]$ for off-standard $A$ as $\sum_C n_C L_C(1)$, where $n_C\ge0$ are actual composition multiplicities. Projecting gives $\sum_{C\in\mathrm{Std}}n_CD_C(1)=0$, and independence forces every such $n_C=0$; the same holds for $e_i$. Exactness extends this to the entire off-standard Serre subcategory. For complex $c$, apply the product of the component projections with entry and residue shift $a\mapsto a-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa$, $n_\kappa=\max_{j\in\kappa}q_j$; its coordinate kernel consists of labels nonstandard in at least one component. A common downward origin shift includes any finitely many labels and residue moves in an admitted cut and does not change $\mathcal O_c$ or the standard predicate.

**Maximal ground-column induction.** Split off the last column, with two-block Levi $\mathfrak g'\oplus\mathfrak g''$ and upper radical $\mathfrak r$, and define $R(X)=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak q)}(\mathbb C_ eta\otimes X)$, $ eta=(0^{N'},(N')^{q_l})$, and right adjoint $H(Y)=\mathbb C_{- eta}\otimes Y^{\mathfrak r}$. PBW gives exact $R$ and $R(N(C') oxtimes N(C''))=N(C)$. The top Levi slice of a simple is its Levi simple: a proper submodule of that slice would generate a proper global submodule by PBW. There are no additional lower $\mathfrak r$-invariants, since moving opposite-radical PBW monomials across the nondegenerate contravariant form pairs a lower invariant to zero against every vector. Hence $H(L(C))=L(C') oxtimes L(C'')$. For a costandard, invariant functionals vanish on all positive-degree opposite-radical monomials, giving $H(
abla(C))=
abla(C') oxtimes
abla(C'')$. Taking the exact top eigenvalue slice of the first-block trace, when $B,C$ have the same degree split, now gives $[N(C):L(B)]=[N(C'):L(B')][N(C''):L(B'')]$: smaller top eigenvalues contribute nothing and the top Levi simple determines its concatenated label uniquely.

**Actual standard embeddings.** Given $C$, shift columns $j\ge2$ upward by integers $k_j\ge0$, chosen successively so each shifted entry in column $j$ exceeds every earlier-column entry in its coset. The resulting $B$ is standard and Bruhat-minimal, hence $N(B)=L(B)$ by [F2]. Write column $j$ of $C$ as $a_{j,1}<\cdots<a_{j,q_j}$ and set $\mathcal E_j=(e_{a_{j,q_j}}\cdots e_{a_{j,q_j}+k_j-1})\cdots(e_{a_{j,1}}\cdots e_{a_{j,1}+k_j-1})$, composing rightmost first. Apply $\mathcal E_2$, then $\mathcal E_3$, through $\mathcal E_l$: the smallest entry is lowered first. In each elementary standard flag, alternative valid lowers occur in earlier columns, hence have strictly smaller prefix Bruhat label. Our desired section is largest and can be moved to the bottom: each adjacent swap splits by the Ext ordering in [F2]. Thus each move gives an actual monomorphism of standards, and exact subsequent residue functors preserve it. Composition gives $N(C)\hookrightarrow\mathcal E_l\cdots\mathcal E_2L(B)$. If $L(A)\hookrightarrow N(C)$, biadjunction gives a surjection from an iterated $f_i$ image of $L(A)$ onto the standard simple $L(B)$; step 1.1 forbids this for off-standard $A$. Every standard therefore has standard-labelled socle.

**An actual cover isomorphism.** Append the ground last column to $B'$. Every $C\ge B$ retains that ground column: a same-coset Bruhat move toward a larger label increases earlier-column sums, so the last-column sum cannot exceed its ground sum, whereas polynomiality makes each last-column entry at least its ground value. Equality forces all of them to be ground; admissibility excludes cross-coset swaps. Thus all $C\ge B$ have degree split $(d',0)$. Adjointness and step 1.2 show that $X=R(P(B')\boxtimes\mathbb C_{c_l+q_l-n})$ has simple head $L(B)$. Lift the cover map to obtain $P(B)\twoheadrightarrow X$, whose image is all of $X$ because it surjects onto its head. By BGG and step 1.2 their standard-flag multiplicities agree in the fixed split and vanish elsewhere. The kernel of this existing epimorphism therefore has every composition multiplicity zero and is zero. Consequently $X\cong P(B)$; an equality of characters has only been used to kill the kernel of an already constructed map.

**The detector and the injective hulls it contains.** The ground simple is projective-injective. Tensoring by $V$ preserves both projectives and injectives because the distinct tensor functor $-\otimes V^*$ is exact and adjoint on both sides. The tensor product contravariant form gives $T\cong DT$. Every simple submodule of a standard-filtered object embeds in one of its successive standard sections, by taking the first section meeting it; hence step 2.1 proves standard socle for every projective and for $T$. Duality gives standard head for $T$. Every standard label of positive degree is $\widetilde f_iB$ for a lower-degree standard label by [F3]; induction using the actual crystal head of $f_iL(B)$ gives $T\twoheadrightarrow L(A)$. Lift this epimorphism through $P(A)\twoheadrightarrow L(A)$; essentiality makes the lift surjective and projectivity splits it. Thus the indecomposable summands of $T$ are exactly the standard-labelled covers, all with positive multiplicity and all injective. Moreover $I(A)=DP(A)\in\operatorname{add}(DT)=\operatorname{add}(T)$ for every standard $A$. This hull membership does not presume individual summand self-duality.

**Cumulative-column projectives.** Put $V_{\le j}=E_1\oplus\cdots\oplus E_j$ and $Z_A=\bigotimes_i\operatorname{Sym}^{a_i}(V_{\le\operatorname{col}(i)})$, with degree $d=\sum_i a_i$, and $Z(A,c)=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathfrak p}^{\mathfrak g}(\mathbb C_{-\rho}\otimes Z_{A,c})$. Induct on the number of columns. One column is completely reducible. Removing the last column and using tensor identity gives $Z(A,c)=R(Z(A',c')\boxtimes\mathbb C_{c_l+q_l-n})\otimes\bigotimes_{i=N-q_l+1}^{N}\operatorname{Sym}^{a_i}(V)$. By induction and step 2.2 the first factor is a sum of actual projective covers. The remaining finite tensor product preserves projectives by its exact distinct-dual adjoint. Polynomial labels form whole blocks: their shared entry multiset cannot admit a below-ground entry, since column strictness would put an entry below the common coset minimum in the bottom row. Thus these ambient projectives lie in the required finite polynomial summand. Every $Z(A,c)$ is genuinely projective.

**Every cover occurs and the quotient has a standard flag.** For a label $B$, take $A=B-A_c$. Project each prefix onto its last-column Levi quotient. The tensor product of the resulting row symmetric powers surjects onto $V(B)$: row symmetrization followed by column antisymmetrization of the row-filled tensor produces a nonzero polynomial highest vector, and Levi complete reducibility gives the simple Schur quotient. Exact induction gives $Z(A,c)\twoheadrightarrow N(B)\twoheadrightarrow L(B)$, and projectivity plus essentiality of the cover makes $P(B)$ a split summand of $Z(A,c)$. Averaging symmetrizers embed $Z_A$ as a $\mathfrak p$-submodule of $V^{\otimes d}$; PBW preserves this injection and identifies the ambient induction with $T$. Its finite $\mathfrak p$-quotient has polynomial Levi simple sections: the radical acts nilpotently by the column filtration, and its invariant subspace in each simple section is Levi-stable and therefore the whole section. Inducing its composition filtration exactly gives a standard flag of $T/Z(A,c)$.

**All-projective copresentations.** For an indecomposable projective $P$, choose a splitting $Z(A,c)=P\oplus Q$ from step 4.1 and view $P$ as its actual submodule of $T$. The sequence $0\to Q\to T/P\to T/Z(A,c)\to0$ gives a standard flag of $T/P$, since $Q$ is projective and has its BGG flag. Its socle is standard by step 2.1, so its finite injective hull $I(T/P)$ belongs to $\operatorname{add}(T)$ by step 3.1. Compose $T\twoheadrightarrow T/P\hookrightarrow I(T/P)$ to obtain $0\to P\to T\to I(T/P)$, exact at $P,T$. Finite sums give every projective a two-step copresentation $0\to P\to T_0\to T_1$ with both $T_i\in\operatorname{add}(T)$. The last arrow need not be surjective.

**The right-adjoint unit.** Choose a full finite projective generator of the entire category-O summand containing $T$ as an explicit summand, with algebra $A$, and let $e$ be the projector onto this actual $T$. Thus $eAe=\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$, retaining all its multiplicities. For $F(X)=eX$, $B=eAe$, the right adjoint is $G_e(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(eA,M)$ with unit $\eta_X(x)(ea)=eax$. The restriction $e\eta_X$ is an isomorphism, so its kernel and cokernel are annihilated by $e$. If $X$ has standard socle then $\eta_X$ is monic. In particular $\eta_T$ is monic and splits since its source $T$ is injective. A complementary summand $C$ has $eC=0$, but adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,G_eFT)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(eC,FT)=0$, forcing its inclusion to vanish and $C=0$. Thus $\eta$ is an isomorphism on $\operatorname{add}(T)$. Apply exact $F$ and left-exact $G_e$ to step 5.1; the comparison of kernels gives $\eta_P$ an isomorphism for every projective. Adjunction therefore proves $F$ fully faithful on all projectives, while left-adjoint recovery has only been asserted on $\operatorname{add}(T)$.

**Tilting full faithfulness.** If $X$ has standard head and $Y$ standard socle, then $\eta_Y$ is monic and its cokernel is annihilated by $e$. Every map from $X$ to that cokernel vanishes: a nonzero image would have a standard simple head because it is a quotient of $X$, while all its factors would be off-standard. By adjunction each $B$-map $FX\to FY$ gives $X\to G_eFY$, which therefore factors uniquely through $Y$. This proves the Hom isomorphism. A tilting's standard flag gives standard socle by step 2.1, and its costandard flag gives standard head by duality. Thus the quotient is fully faithful on all tiltings.

**The actual Whittaker comparison and quotient.** By [F1] the exact Whittaker functor factors through $F$ as the actual equivalence $U\otimes_B-$, with $U$ a right $B$-progenerator and $W_d=\operatorname{End}_B(U)$. Its inverse is $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,-)$, and its unit on $FX$ is $m\mapsto(u\mapsto u\otimes m)$. Under the source action this is precisely $\gamma_X(f)=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}(f)j^{-1}$, since the counit on $T\otimes_B FX$ is evaluation; thus the comparison is a natural isomorphism of actual maps and Hecke modules. In particular $U$ is a left $W_d$-progenerator, and $V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}$ is fully faithful on projectives by step 6.1. The corner functor $F$ is the Serre quotient with kernel consisting of objects with only off-standard factors; applying the genuine equivalence identifies the same quotient for $V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}$. Projectivity is preserved on $\operatorname{add}(T)$, whose image consists of the corresponding projective covers. This does not assert preservation for other ambient projectives.

**Simple images and standard heads.** The exact corner functor kills precisely off-standard simples and identifies its other simple images with the distinct exhaustive $B$-simples; the genuine equivalence of step 8.1 transports these to the corresponding finite-W simples $L_W(A)$. For standard $A$, $P(A)\in\operatorname{add}(T)$, so $\pi P(A)$ is an indecomposable $B$-projective with head $\pi L(A)$: its Hom to each simple is the corresponding Hom from $P(A)$ by the elementary add$(T)$ equivalence. Lift $P(A)\to L(A)$ through $N(A)\to L(A)$; the image surjects onto the standard's head and is therefore the whole standard. Applying exact $\pi$ makes $\pi N(A)$ a nonzero quotient of this indecomposable projective, so it has the same unique simple head. Through Morita, the actual finite-Levi standard $V(A)=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}N(A)$ likewise has unique simple head $L_W(A)$. This does not assert that a specified finite-Levi highest vector generates it.

**Independent row compression.** Add $t$ full ground rows until the enlarged smallest column has height at least $d$; all roots $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ remain fixed. For each row $r$, the normalized coefficient $D_r^{(1)}$ is its row-Cartan operator, with ground scalar $\kappa_r=\sum_{j:\,r\text{ lies in column }j}c_j$. On the actual tensor space and every finite-Levi standard of degree $d$ its eigenvalues are $\kappa_r+h$, $0\le h\le d$, since the remaining weight is polynomial row occupancy. Thus the SAME finite-image element $e=\prod_{r\text{ deleted}}\prod_{h=1}^{d}(1-(D_r^{(1)}-\kappa_r)/h)$ is the zero-deleted-occupancy projector on both tensor space and all these standards. In $U^+$ it selects tensors using only retained rows. The actual dot formula preserves row multisets, so $e$ commutes with dots and crossings and belongs to the left image by the independent raw first centralizer of [F1]. Each right matrix restricts identically under the retained-box embedding: left neighbours and row/column indices agree and its scalar $a_j$ is unchanged. Therefore $eU^+=U$ as right Hecke modules. Extending a commuting endomorphism of $eU^+$ by zero shows $eA^+e=A$, where $A^+,A$ are the large and small left image algebras. For the finite-Levi standard, the zero-deleted-occupancy part of $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j+t})$ is $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j})$ by its tensor Young-symmetrizer realization, and vanishes exactly when a deleted-row partition entry is nonzero. In the original path expansion, Levi projection kills off-column factors and each surviving strictly-forward path has at most one factor in each column. A deleted intermediate row changes removed-coordinate occupancy in a column with no later factor there to undo it; compression therefore kills that monomial. Remaining paths are exactly the small paths. The head shift in column $j$ changes by $-(j-1)t$, cancelling the retained source-reading shift $+(j-1)t$; its normalized highest weight remains the entry plus row index minus one. The corner action and its Gauss coefficients consequently give $eV(A^+)=V(A)$ for contractible labels and zero for noncontractible labels, as actual module identifications.

**Simple contraction without highest-vector assumptions.** Every noncontractible standard simple is killed by $e$, because it is a quotient of the standard annihilated in step 9.2. For a finite algebra and an idempotent $e$, restriction gives a bijection between its simple modules surviving $e$ and the simples of $eAe$: any nonzero vector in $eL$ generates $eL=eAe v$, and for a small simple $M$ the module $Ae\otimes_{eAe}M$ has a unique simple quotient surviving $e$. Indeed its $e$-part is $M$; every proper submodule has zero $e$-part, since a submodule containing that part generates the whole induced module. The sum of all such proper submodules is still annihilated by $e$ and is the unique maximal submodule. Apply this to the independent corner in step 9.2. By step 9.1 both simple lists are complete, and small standard labels are in bijection with contractible large standard labels by adjoining full ground rows. Thus the survivors form a subset of the contractible list with exactly the same finite cardinality, so every contractible simple survives. Its restriction is a simple quotient of $eV(A^+)=V(A)$, which has the unique head from step 9.1, hence $eL_W(A^+)=L_W(A)$.

**Fullness and the central Hecke corner.** If a contractible $A^+$ and another label have the same entry-multiset central character, admissibility separates charge cosets and identifies all charges within each coset. Its minimal bottom entry $c_j+1-(n+t)$ appears in each column of that coset; strictness and nonnegative ground differences force the same entries into the bottom row of the other label. Remove that row and repeat for every deleted row. Thus the contractible labels form a union of whole central-character blocks. Let $f$ be their central support in $A^+$; then $e=ef=fe$, since $e$ kills all complementary simples. Every simple of $A_f=fA^+f$ survives $e$ by step 10.1. If $A_feA_f$ were proper, its nonzero quotient would have a simple killed by $e$, a contradiction. Hence $f=\sum_k a_keb_k$. Multiplication $A_fe\otimes_{eA_fe}eM\to M$ has inverse $m\mapsto\sum_k a_ke\otimes eb_km$; balancing and this identity verify both composites. This gives a faithful Morita equivalence on all supported-block modules. The operator $f$ belongs to the right centralizer and is central there, so restriction identifies $fB^+f=\operatorname{End}_{A_f}(fU^+)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $B=\operatorname{End}_{eA_fe}(eU^+)^{\mathrm{op}}$. To verify enlarged stable faithfulness directly, choose $d$ distinct terminal boxes on length-$l$ Jordan strings. In the associated graded tensor action each bounded PBW word $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w$, $0\le a_i<l$, sends their ordered terminal tensor to the tensor in which those distinct strings have been permuted by $w$ and the box on string $i$ moved $a_i$ places left. These $l^dd!$ outputs are distinct basis tensors, so the graded PBW word images are linearly independent. A nonzero filtered Hecke element has a nonzero leading PBW symbol; graded injectivity makes its leading operator nonzero, hence its actual operator is nonzero. The enlarged stable action is therefore faithful, giving $B=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$. Its trace is therefore symmetric and nondegenerate by [F4]. This local proof precedes, and does not depend on, a later stable-range definition.

**The actual duality comparison.** Let $\beta:T\to DT$ be the tensor contravariant form. Put $\delta M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,T)$ with $(bf)(m)=f(m)b^*$, and $X^\#=\operatorname{Hom}_{B}(X,B)$ with the same twist. Transposition gives the natural isomorphism $\delta M\to\pi DM$, $f\mapsto Df\circ\beta$, whose inverse is $g\mapsto\beta^{-1}\circ Dg\circ\operatorname{bidual}_M$. This uses only $T\cong DT$, not individual projective self-duality. Tensor-Hom gives $\delta\pi^*\cong\#$, and the symmetric trace of step 11.1 gives $\#\cong D_B$ by $h\mapsto\operatorname{tr}\circ h$. Define $\theta_M:M\to D\pi^*\delta M$ by $\theta_M(m)(t\otimes f)=(t,f(m))$. The form identity $(xtb,t')=(t,x^{\mathrm{tr}}t'b^*)$ makes this balanced and $\mathfrak g$-linear. Applying $\pi$ gives a natural map $\pi\to\pi D\pi^*\delta\cong\#\pi D$ between exact functors; exactness of $\#$ follows from the symmetric algebra's injective regular module. On $T$ it is the regular trace-duality isomorphism, and hence is invertible on add$(T)$. Use the copresentations of step 5.1 and kernels to prove it invertible on every projective; use finite projective presentations and cokernels to prove it invertible on every object. Dualizing gives the genuine module isomorphism $\pi D\cong D_B\pi$.

**Individual standard prinjectives are self-dual.** For standard $A$, $I(A)=DP(A)\in\operatorname{add}(T)$ by step 3.1. Step 12.1 gives $\pi I(A)=D_B\pi P(A)$ and fixes its simple label because $DL(A)=L(A)$. In a symmetric algebra the primitive projective $Be_A$ is also the injective hull of its corresponding simple: the perfect trace identifies its linear dual with the corresponding right ideal, and the $*$ twist sends the primitive to the primitive carrying the dual simple. Since that simple is fixed here, $D_B\pi P(A)\cong\pi P(A)$. Both $I(A)$ and $P(A)$ are projectives, so full faithfulness of step 6.1 lifts this isomorphism and its inverse; their composites are identities by faithfulness. Hence $I(A)\cong P(A)$, so each standard projective-injective is individually self-dual. This last conclusion has been derived after the copresentation, central-corner and duality constructions, and was not used to prove them.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For admissible origins $c$ the genuine Whittaker functor $V$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] is exact
on $\mathcal O_c^d$, and
$$\gamma\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{W}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(-))$$
is a natural isomorphism, where $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Both $V$ and the
Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ are fully faithful on
all projective objects of the relevant summand, and the quotient is also fully
faithful on tiltings. $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detecting object
containing all standard-labelled projective-injective covers, each individually self-dual, but it need not be a
generator of the entire category-$\mathcal O$ summand. $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$
is a projective generator of $W_d$-mod, and $V$ preserves projectivity on
$\operatorname{add}(T)$; it need not send every projective of $\mathcal O$ to
a projective $W$-module. The composite of $V$ with the Morita equivalence is
the Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines finite tensoring, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,
$Q_\chi$ and $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ be as in
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the
exact functor
$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$
on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a
$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$
is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms
$(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible,
and for the one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting
isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$
is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.

Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every label $A$ in a
genuine tableau parabolic block of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins
with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.
Equivalently, $T(A)$ has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$. Every tilting object is a finite
direct sum of these, and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis.
Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing
$A$ the corresponding partial tilting is the same ambient $T(A)$, since all
support labels are $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each
finite block, with flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a
bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability and maximal support.
In the inline prinjectivity claim, $P(A)$ is projective-injective (equivalently
self-dual) exactly when $A$ is standard; in that case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$
with the proved rectification label.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. A set of representatives suffices: every finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)$-module is a quotient of some $U(\mathfrak g)^n$, and those quotients form a set up to isomorphism.

Define the formal character by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_\mu(\dim M_\mu)e^\mu$. By [[prop-equivalent-support-description-of-category-o]], its integer coefficients are finite and supported in finitely many downward cones. Let $\mathscr R$ be the group of all such integer coefficient families, with pointwise addition. It is a ring with $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$: at a fixed resulting weight, in any pair of cones the equation $\beta+\gamma=\eta$ with $\beta,\gamma\in Q^+$ has finitely many solutions, since every simple-root coefficient is bounded. Taking weight spaces is exact, so character gives a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(\mathcal O)\to\mathscr R$. The zero object's class and character are zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For admissible origins $c$ the genuine Whittaker functor $V$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] is exact
on $\mathcal O_c^d$, and
$$\gamma\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{W}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(-))$$
is a natural isomorphism, where $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Both $V$ and the
Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ are fully faithful on
all projective objects of the relevant summand, and the quotient is also fully
faithful on tiltings. $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detecting object
containing all standard-labelled projective-injective covers, each individually self-dual, but it need not be a
generator of the entire category-$\mathcal O$ summand. $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$
is a projective generator of $W_d$-mod, and $V$ preserves projectivity on
$\operatorname{add}(T)$; it need not send every projective of $\mathcal O$ to
a projective $W$-module. The composite of $V$ with the Morita equivalence is
the Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples.

derivations.claim: Exactness of $\pi_\alpha$. $T_\alpha$ is a direct summand of the projective object $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ by [F1]; $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P,-)$ is exact for projective $P$, and passing to a direct summand preserves exactness, so $\pi_\alpha$ is exact.

The left adjoint. The tensor-Hom adjunction gives $\pi^*_\alpha=T_\alpha\otimes_{B_\alpha}-$ as left adjoint of $\pi_\alpha$; tensoring with a right module is right exact but not left exact in general, and the rank-one witness exhibits the failure of exactness. Free $B_\alpha$-modules map to direct sums of copies of $T_\alpha$, which are projective, and direct summands of projective objects are projective, so $\pi^*_\alpha$ sends $B_\alpha$-projectives to projectives.

The whole-summand generator. By [F4], the finite sum $G_d$ is projective and contains every Col-labelled cover; exact central projection gives the projective generator $G_\alpha$ of the whole block. The same supplier gives actual inclusions of each prefix summand in $T_d$ with standard-filtered quotients, providing the projective-copresentation prerequisite without identifying $G_\alpha$ with the detector $T_\alpha$.

Recovery on $\operatorname{add}(T_\alpha)$. The evaluation $\pi^*_\alpha\pi_\alpha(T_\alpha)=T_\alpha\otimes_{B_\alpha}\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)\to T_\alpha$ is an isomorphism by the endomorphism-algebra description [F2] (the standard evaluation of a free rank-one module), and for direct summands it follows by restriction of idempotents; hence $\pi^*_\alpha\pi_\alpha$ recovers every object of $\operatorname{add}(T_\alpha)$, in particular every standard-labelled prinjective contained in $T_\alpha$.

The boundaries. The rank-one two-equal-charge example shows that $\pi^*_\alpha$ is not exact and that $\pi^*_\alpha\pi_\alpha$ does not return every projective of the ambient category: the dominant projective maps to the simple over $\mathbb C[x]/x^2$, and its image under $\pi^*\pi$ is the costandard object $T/xT$, not the projective. Both failures are recorded as boundaries and are not repaired by changing the conventions.

Assembly. Since the charges decompose $T$ into finitely many central components in each degree and the categories are locally unital in the infinite case, the functors $\pi_\alpha$ assemble to the locally unital sum; the ambient category retains all labels, including those killed by the functors.
